title: 119. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Converting Metric Length Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a length given in metres to centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(5\text{ m}\) to \(\text{cm}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}\), multiply \(5\) by \(100\): \(5 \times 100 = 500\). Therefore, \(5\text{ m}=500\text{ cm}\). The alternative \(50\text{ cm}\) uses a conversion factor that differs by a factor of \(10\) from the required factor; it does not represent the same physical quantity as \(500\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Identify whether the target length unit is larger or smaller.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a length given in centimetres to metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(300\text{ cm}\) to \(\text{m}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(100\text{ cm}=1\text{ m}\), divide \(300\) by \(100\): \(300 \div 100 = 3\). Therefore, \(300\text{ cm}=3\text{ m}\). The alternative \(30\text{ m}\) uses a conversion factor that differs by a factor of \(10\) from the required factor; it does not represent the same physical quantity as \(3\text{ m}\).
questions.hint: Choose a conversion direction that cancels the original length unit.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a length given in kilometres to metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(2.5\text{ km}\) to \(\text{m}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ km}=1{,}000\text{ m}\), multiply \(2.5\) by \(1{,}000\): \(2.5 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}500\). Therefore, \(2.5\text{ km}=2{,}500\text{ m}\). The alternative \(250\text{ m}\) uses a conversion factor that differs by a factor of \(10\) from the required factor; it does not represent the same physical quantity as \(2{,}500\text{ m}\).
questions.hint: Use the metric prefixes to compare the two length units.
